units.title: What COBOL Is and Where It Runs
units.tip: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) was invented in 1959 to handle business data processing. It remains in use today for financial systems, government agencies, and large corporations handling very large volumes of money and records.

exercises.question: What does COBOL stand for?
exercises.answer: Common Business-Oriented Language
exercises.explain: COBOL was designed in 1959 specifically for business and administrative systems that process large amounts of data.

exercises.question: What decade was COBOL invented?
exercises.explain: COBOL was developed in 1959 and first standardized in 1961, making it one of the oldest high-level languages still in use.

exercises.question: For what type of work was COBOL designed?
exercises.answer: Business data processing and administration
exercises.explain: COBOL was created to solve business problems like payroll, inventory, and financial record-keeping, not scientific computing.

exercises.question: Which of these sectors is COBOL still widely used in today?
exercises.answer: Banking and government
exercises.explain: Legacy COBOL systems handle enormous financial transactions and government records because replacing them would be too costly and risky.

exercises.question: Why has COBOL remained in use for over 60 years?
exercises.answer: It is stable, reliable, and replacing it would be extremely expensive
exercises.explain: Huge amounts of working COBOL code run mission-critical data. Rewriting those systems in modern languages is costly and risky.
choices: It is stable, reliable, and replacing it would be extremely expensive
It is easier to learn than Java
It is more powerful than modern languages
It is required by law in all countries

exercises.question: What is a COBOL program?
exercises.answer: A file containing one or more divisions of code
exercises.explain: A COBOL program is organized into divisions, each serving a specific purpose in the overall structure.
choices: A file containing one or more divisions of code
A single section with all code mixed together
A web application written in COBOL

exercises.question: How many main divisions does COBOL have?
exercises.answer: Four
exercises.explain: COBOL has four divisions: IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT, DATA, and PROCEDURE. Each serves a distinct purpose.

exercises.question: Which division describes the program's name and purpose?
exercises.answer: IDENTIFICATION
exercises.explain: The IDENTIFICATION division contains metadata like the program name, author, and date of creation.

exercises.question: Is the order of divisions in a COBOL program flexible?
exercises.answer: No, they must appear in a fixed order
exercises.explain: COBOL requires divisions in this exact order: IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT, DATA, PROCEDURE. Changing the order causes a syntax error.
choices: No, they must appear in a fixed order

exercises.question: Which division must come last in a COBOL program?
exercises.answer: PROCEDURE
exercises.explain: The fixed order is IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT, DATA, PROCEDURE, so the executable statements in PROCEDURE come last.

units.title: The Four Divisions
units.tip: Each COBOL division has a specific role. IDENTIFICATION tells what the program is. ENVIRONMENT tells it where files and hardware are. DATA defines the structure of data. PROCEDURE contains the actual instructions.

exercises.question: What information goes in the IDENTIFICATION division?
exercises.answer: Program name, author, date, and purpose
exercises.explain: The IDENTIFICATION division is metadata. It includes PROGRAM-ID, AUTHOR, DATE-WRITTEN, and other descriptive paragraphs.
choices: Program name, author, date, and purpose

exercises.question: Which paragraph is required in the IDENTIFICATION division?
exercises.answer: PROGRAM-ID
exercises.explain: PROGRAM-ID is mandatory; it gives the program a name. Other paragraphs like AUTHOR and DATE-WRITTEN are optional.

exercises.question: What is the purpose of the ENVIRONMENT division?
exercises.answer: To declare files and input/output devices
exercises.explain: The ENVIRONMENT division maps logical file names to physical files, tapes, and hardware devices.
choices: To declare files and input/output devices

exercises.question: What section of the ENVIRONMENT division defines how files are used?
exercises.answer: INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION
exercises.explain: The INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION contains the FILE-CONTROL paragraph that links logical file names to physical files.

exercises.question: Where in the ENVIRONMENT division would you declare that a file is on disk?
exercises.answer: In FILE-CONTROL paragraph under INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION
exercises.explain: FILE-CONTROL uses SELECT ... ASSIGN entries to link each logical file name to a physical file or device.
choices: In FILE-CONTROL paragraph under INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION

exercises.question: What is the purpose of the DATA division?
exercises.answer: To define the structure and format of all data used by the program
exercises.explain: The DATA division declares every variable, file record, and work area the program will use, with their types and sizes.
choices: To define the structure and format of all data used by the program

exercises.question: Which section of the DATA division describes file record layouts?
exercises.answer: FILE SECTION
exercises.explain: The FILE SECTION defines the structure of records in each file declared in ENVIRONMENT division.

exercises.question: What is WORKING-STORAGE SECTION?
exercises.answer: Variables and temporary storage used by the program
exercises.explain: WORKING-STORAGE holds variables created and used during program execution, separate from file data.
choices: Variables and temporary storage used by the program
Input parameters from the operating system

exercises.question: What does the PROCEDURE division contain?
exercises.answer: The executable statements and logic of the program
exercises.explain: The PROCEDURE division holds the actual verbs (MOVE, PERFORM, READ, etc.) that make the program do its work.
choices: The executable statements and logic of the program

exercises.question: How is the PROCEDURE division organized?
exercises.answer: Into paragraphs and sections containing named procedures
exercises.explain: PROCEDURE division code is split into named paragraphs (like MAIN, PROCESS-RECORDS) that can be called with PERFORM.
choices: Into a single block of code
Into paragraphs and sections containing named procedures

units.title: Data Definition and PIC Clauses
units.tip: Data items in COBOL are defined with PIC (picture) clauses that describe their format. Numeric items use 9, alphabetic use A, alphanumeric use X. The clause tells COBOL how to store and display data.

exercises.question: What does PIC stand for in COBOL?
exercises.answer: Picture clause
exercises.explain: PIC is short for PICTURE, which describes the format and size of a data item.

exercises.question: In a PIC clause, what does the character '9' represent?
exercises.answer: A numeric digit (0-9)
exercises.explain: PIC 9 means one numeric digit. PIC 999 means a three-digit number. PIC 9(5) means five numeric digits.

exercises.question: What PIC clause defines an alphabetic field?
exercises.answer: PIC A
exercises.explain: PIC A allows only letters and spaces. PIC A(10) allows 10 such characters. Digits and special characters are not allowed.

exercises.question: What PIC clause allows any character (letters, numbers, symbols)?
exercises.answer: PIC X
exercises.explain: PIC X is alphanumeric. PIC X(20) allows 20 characters of any type.

exercises.question: Which PIC clause uses a repeat count to define a 5-digit number?
exercises.answer: PIC 9(5)
exercises.explain: PIC 9(5) means five numeric digits. The parentheses are a repeat count for the 9.

exercises.question: What is a 'data level' in COBOL?
exercises.answer: A number indicating how data items relate hierarchically
exercises.explain: Data levels (01, 05, 10, etc.) show nesting. Level 01 is the top group; higher numbers are sub-items.
choices: A number indicating how data items relate hierarchically
The number of digits a variable holds
How many times a variable is used

exercises.question: What does level '01' represent in COBOL data?
exercises.answer: A top-level record or group item
exercises.explain: Level 01 is the highest level, usually a complete record. All other levels are subordinate to it.
choices: A top-level record or group item

exercises.question: How do you create a sub-field within a record?
exercises.answer: Use a higher data level number (05, 10, etc.) for nested items
exercises.explain: If a level-01 record contains a customer address, the street, city, state would be level-05 items.
choices: Use a higher data level number (05, 10, etc.) for nested items

exercises.question: In COBOL, can a level-05 item belong to two different level-01 records?
exercises.answer: No, it belongs only to the nearest higher-level item
exercises.explain: A level-05 belongs to the most recent level-01 or other parent level above it.
choices: No, it belongs only to the nearest higher-level item

exercises.question: What is a 'group item' in COBOL?
exercises.answer: A data item that contains multiple sub-items
exercises.explain: A group item (like an address) has no PIC clause; it is composed of smaller fields (street, city, state).
choices: A data item that contains multiple sub-items

units.title: The PROCEDURE Division and Basic Operations
units.tip: The PROCEDURE division is where the actual work happens. It reads data, processes it, performs calculations, and writes results. The basic structure uses paragraphs that can be called by PERFORM.

exercises.question: What does the MOVE verb do in COBOL?
exercises.answer: Copies a value from one variable to another
exercises.explain: MOVE copies data. The source keeps its value; the destination gets a copy. Example: MOVE employee-name TO report-name
choices: Copies a value from one variable to another

exercises.question: What happens when you MOVE a shorter value to a longer field?
exercises.answer: The shorter value is padded with spaces (or zeros for numeric fields)
exercises.explain: COBOL adjusts the length. Text is left-aligned and padded right with spaces; numbers are right-aligned and padded left with zeros.
choices: The shorter value is padded with spaces (or zeros for numeric fields)

exercises.question: Which verb adds two numbers in COBOL?
exercises.answer: ADD
exercises.explain: ADD adds values. Example: ADD hours-worked TO total-hours

exercises.question: How do you subtract in COBOL?
exercises.answer: SUBTRACT
exercises.explain: SUBTRACT subtracts one value from another. Example: SUBTRACT deductions FROM gross-pay GIVING net-pay

exercises.question: What is the MULTIPLY verb used for?
exercises.answer: To multiply two values together
exercises.explain: MULTIPLY multiplies values. Example: MULTIPLY price BY quantity GIVING total

exercises.question: What does the PERFORM verb do?
exercises.answer: Calls a named paragraph or section
exercises.explain: PERFORM jumps to a paragraph, executes it, and returns. It is similar to a function call in other languages.
choices: Calls a named paragraph or section

exercises.question: What does PERFORM ... UNTIL do?
exercises.answer: Repeats a paragraph until a condition is true
exercises.explain: PERFORM ... UNTIL loops, executing the paragraph repeatedly until the condition becomes true.
choices: Repeats a paragraph until a condition is true
Performs only if a condition is false

exercises.question: What happens after a PERFORM completes?
exercises.answer: Control returns to the statement after the PERFORM
exercises.explain: PERFORM calls a paragraph and waits for it to finish, then continues with the next statement.
choices: Control returns to the statement after the PERFORM

exercises.question: How do you execute a paragraph 10 times in COBOL?
exercises.answer: PERFORM paragraph-name 10 TIMES
exercises.explain: This syntax tells COBOL to call the paragraph exactly 10 times.

exercises.question: What does PERFORM VARYING do?
exercises.answer: Repeats a paragraph while incrementing a counter variable
exercises.explain: PERFORM VARYING is like a for-loop, incrementing a variable each time until a condition is met.
choices: Varies the data in a file
Repeats a paragraph while incrementing a counter variable

units.title: Conditionals and Decision Making
units.tip: COBOL uses IF statements to make decisions based on conditions. You can test equality, inequality, and numeric comparisons. Conditions can be combined with AND, OR, and NOT.

exercises.question: What is the basic structure of an IF statement in COBOL?
exercises.answer: IF condition THEN statement(s) ELSE statement(s) END-IF
exercises.explain: IF checks a condition. If true, the first statements execute. If false, the ELSE statements execute (if present).
choices: IF condition THEN statement(s) ELSE statement(s) END-IF

exercises.question: How do you test if two values are equal in COBOL?
exercises.answer: IF value1 = value2
exercises.explain: The = operator tests equality. Example: IF employee-salary = 50000

exercises.question: How do you test if a value is greater than another?
exercises.answer: IF value1 > value2
exercises.explain: The > operator tests if the first value is greater. < tests less than, = tests equal.

exercises.question: How do you combine two conditions with AND in COBOL?
exercises.answer: IF condition1 AND condition2
exercises.explain: AND requires both conditions to be true. If either is false, the whole condition is false.

exercises.question: What does OR do in a COBOL condition?
exercises.answer: Makes the condition true if either condition is true
exercises.explain: OR requires at least one condition to be true. If either is true, the whole condition is true.
choices: Makes the condition true if either condition is true

exercises.question: How do you test if a value is NOT equal in COBOL?
exercises.answer: IF value1 NOT = value2
exercises.explain: NOT placed before the relational operator reverses it, so NOT = means not equal.

exercises.question: Can IF statements be nested inside each other?
exercises.answer: Yes, one IF can be inside another IF
exercises.explain: Nested IFs allow complex decision trees. An IF inside an IF's THEN or ELSE clause executes conditionally.
choices: No, only one IF per program
Yes, one IF can be inside another IF

exercises.question: What does EVALUATE do in COBOL?
exercises.answer: Tests one value against multiple conditions (like a switch statement)
exercises.explain: EVALUATE works like a switch or case statement and is cleaner than many nested IFs when testing one value against many.
choices: Tests one value against multiple conditions (like a switch statement)

exercises.question: Which statement tests that WS-COUNT is less than 10?
exercises.answer: IF WS-COUNT < 10
exercises.explain: The < operator tests less than. COBOL also accepts IS LESS THAN.

exercises.question: What does 'END-IF' do in COBOL?
exercises.answer: Marks the end of an IF statement block
exercises.explain: END-IF clearly closes the IF statement, making code more readable, especially with nested IFs.
choices: Marks the end of an IF statement block

units.title: Files, Records, and I/O
units.tip: COBOL reads and writes files containing records. A file is declared in ENVIRONMENT, its structure in DATA, and READ/WRITE operations happen in PROCEDURE. Sequential files are processed one record at a time.

exercises.question: What is a 'record' in COBOL?
exercises.answer: A collection of related fields treated as one unit
exercises.explain: A record (like an employee record) groups fields (name, salary, ID) together. Each file contains one or more records.
choices: A collection of related fields treated as one unit

exercises.question: What is a 'sequential file' in COBOL?
exercises.answer: Records stored in order, must be read one after another
exercises.explain: In a sequential file, you read the first record, then the second, then the third, in order. You cannot jump to record 10.
choices: A file that can be accessed randomly
A file that cannot be written to
A file that stores only numbers
Records stored in order, must be read one after another

exercises.question: Where is a file's structure defined in COBOL?
exercises.answer: In the FILE SECTION of the DATA division
exercises.explain: FILE SECTION describes the layout and fields of each record in a file.
choices: In the FILE SECTION of the DATA division

exercises.question: What does 'FD' stand for in COBOL file definitions?
exercises.answer: File Description
exercises.explain: FD introduces a file description entry. It is followed by the file name and then the record layout.

exercises.question: Can a file have multiple record types with different structures?
exercises.answer: Yes, with several 01 record descriptions under the FD or with REDEFINES
exercises.explain: A file might have header records, detail records, and trailer records with different layouts.
choices: No, all records must be identical
Yes, with several 01 record descriptions under the FD or with REDEFINES

exercises.question: What does the READ verb do?
exercises.answer: Reads the next record from a file into memory
exercises.explain: READ fetches one record from the current file position. After reading, you can process it.
choices: Displays a record on the screen
Deletes a record from a file
Reads the next record from a file into memory

exercises.question: What does the WRITE verb do?
exercises.answer: Outputs a record to a file
exercises.explain: WRITE sends a record from working storage to an output file.
choices: Outputs a record to a file

exercises.question: What is the 'AT END' clause in a READ statement?
exercises.answer: Specifies what to do when the file ends
exercises.explain: AT END executes if READ tries to read past the last record (end-of-file). Example: READ input-file AT END MOVE 1 TO eof-flag
choices: The last record in the file
Specifies what to do when the file ends
The file location at the end

exercises.question: How do you process all records in a file?
exercises.answer: READ the first record, then PERFORM a loop UNTIL the end-of-file flag is set
exercises.explain: Read the first record before the loop. In the loop, process the record and READ the next one, setting a flag in AT END, until the flag is set.
choices: READ the first record, then PERFORM a loop UNTIL the end-of-file flag is set

exercises.question: What verb closes a file in COBOL?
exercises.answer: CLOSE
exercises.explain: CLOSE flushes any buffered data and releases the file. Always close files when done with them.
